h: Stones, Stars and a Pretty Village Stop
p: Getting to Dalby is part of the adventure. The forest drive winds in through the trees, and there's a charge to take the car through, so factor that into your plans. The main visitor area at Low Dalby is the natural base for the day, with paths and trails heading off in all directions.

Treat your Go Ape slot as the centrepiece and allow a couple of hours for it once you count the kit-up and briefing. Morning sessions are a good shout, leaving the afternoon free to explore, and if you're coming a fair distance it's worth checking the forecast the night before, as the Moors can be a lot wilder than the coast.

Walkers shouldn't miss the Bridestones, a cluster of odd, weathered sandstone outcrops looked after by the National Trust, reached by a lovely moorland walk from the forest. Further along the Pickering to Whitby road, the Hole of Horcum is a huge natural hollow in the moors that's a great spot for a breezy stomp and a big view.

On the way in or out, Thornton-le-Dale is one of those chocolate-box villages with a stream running alongside the main street and cottages you'll want to photograph. Scarborough and the coast are close enough to round the trip off with fish and chips on the front, which is never a bad way to finish a day in the trees.
